title: P300 dataset BI2014b from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
description: EEG recordings from 38 healthy participants playing in pairs the multi-user version of Brain Invaders, a visual P300-based brain-computer interface using an oddball paradigm on a grid of 36 symbols. Data were collected with 32 wet electrodes per subject across three randomized conditions (Solo1, Solo2, Collaboration) to study inter-brain synchrony in collaborative BCI. The experiment was conducted at GIPSA-lab, Grenoble, France, in 2014.
methods_description: Pairs of participants played Brain Invaders 2 in three randomized conditions: Solo1, Solo2, and Collaboration. Each game session had 9 levels with predefined alien configurations, and flashes were delivered in pseudo-random groups of 6 symbols (1:5 target to non-target ratio). EEG was recorded at 512 Hz with g.USBamp amplifiers and 32 Ag/AgCl wet electrodes per subject, referenced to the right earlobe with ground at Fz. Triggers were synchronized via a USB analog-to-digital converter. An adaptive Riemannian minimum-distance-to-mean classifier gave online feedback. In the solo conditions the non-playing participant watched a cross, which controls for fake inter-brain synchrony.
